full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq J: The claim of the petitioner is pivoted on section 498 of Code of Criminal Procedure (shortly the Code) and petitioner knocks at the door of this court craving for Anticipatory Bail in anticipation of arrest in connection with Kulshi Police Station Non First Information Report Case No. 263 of 2001 corresponding to Non GR Case No. 2033 of 2001 under sections 465/467/468/ 469/471/506 and 34 of Penal Code pending in the court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 The provision for bail, in a criminal case beginning from the initiation of proceeding upon the conclusion of the trial has been made in Chapter XXXIX of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is well settled that the basic conception of the word 'bail' is release of a person from the custody of police and delivery into the hands of sureties, who undertake to produce him in Court whenever required to do so. An accused person is said, at common law, to be admitted to bail, when he is released from the custody of the officers of the court and is entrusted to the custody of persons known as his sureties who are bound to produce him to answer at a specified time and place the charge against him and who in default of so doing are liable to forfeit such sum as is specified when bail is granted. 

 19. Meaning and definition of Bail stated in the foregoing paragraphs indicate that there is not much of difference between 'Bail' and "Anticipatory Bail". The only distinction between 'Bail' and "Anticipatory Bail" is that whereas the former is granted after arrest and therefore, means release from custody and the latter is granted in anticipation of arrest and the power is exercisable in case of an anticipated accusation of an offence and is effective at the very moment of arrest. 

 20. The Code of Criminal Procedure 1998 originally did not contain an specific provision for Anticipator; Bail. By Ordinance XLIX of 1978, provision of Anticipatory Bail has been provided on insertion of section 497 A in the Code. The inserted section 497 A postulated that when any person had reason to believe that he might be arrested on an accusation of having committed a nonbailable offence he might apply to the High Court Division or the Court of Session or the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for a direction under this section, and that Court or the Magistrate might, if it or he thought fit, direct that in the event of such arrest, he would be released on bail. Section 497 A empowered the High Court Division or the Court of Session or the Sub-Divisional Magistrate to include such conditions in the direction under sub-section (I) in the light of the fact of the particular case as it might think fit. By Ordinance No. IX of 1982, the provision of Anticipatory Bail embodied in section 497A by Ordinance No. XLIX of 1978 stood omitted. The Code now does not contain any provision of Anticipatory Bail. The Law Commission of India in its 41st Report pointed out the necessity of introducing a provision in the Code enabling High Court and Court of Sessions to grant Anticipatory Bail. In compliance of the Report of Law Commission amendments have been brought about in the Code in Indian Jurisdiction and on insertion of section 438 provisions for Anticipatory Bail with positive condition had been made. In our country although provision for granting anticipatory bail has not been made in the Code through judicial pronouncements but scope and law of Anticipatory Bail have been set out. In State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury and another 51 DLR (AD) 242=4 MLR (AD) 291 an observation has been recorded by Appellate Division in the terms that since there is a Law Commission in Bangladesh the matter may be referred by the Government before the Law Commission for incorporating a section in the Code of Criminal Procedure for granting anticipatory bail as has been done by the Law Commission of India by inserting section 438 in the Indian Criminal Procedure Code. By such legislation there will be a specific statutory sanction of granting anticipatory bail with positive conditions and directions. But till now no step appears to have been taken by the Law Commission in the light of observation made by the Appellate Division. 

 21. Consideration which should weigh with the court while dealing with a request for anticipatory bail need not be the same as for an application to release on bail after arrest. In granting anticipatory bail the judicial discretion must be properly exercised after proper application of mind to decide whether the case is fit one for granting anticipatory bail or not. 

 23. Therefore, although the powers are wide the judicial discretion would impose self-restraint but it would depend upon fact and circumstances of the case. 

 25. In Muhammad Ayub vs Md. Yakub, 19 DLR (SC) 38 it has been held-Section 498 would be called in aid before the Court of Sessions and the High Court even where the Court is not seized directly of the proceeding in question and where no actual arrest has been made so far but anticipatory bail is asked for e.g. where the case is still at a stage of investigation by the police or pending in a subordinate court. 

 Anticipatory bail is an extraordinary remedy, and an exception to the general law of bail which can be granted only in extraordinary and exceptional circumstances upon a proper and intelligent exercise of discretion. Generally speaking, the main circumstances as would entitle an order for extraordinary remedy of pre-arrest bail is the perception of the court upon the facts and materials disclosed by the petitioner before it that the criminal proceeding which is being or has been launched against him is being or has been taken with an ulterior motive, political Or otherwise, for harassing the accused and not for securing justice in a particular case. 

 The only other case where the prayer may also be considered may occur if it is proved that on account of some local public commotion or other circumstances it is not possible for the petitioner to appear before the lower court for seeking bail. The petitioner must, however, remain physically present in court before his application for bail can be entertained. Ordinarily, when a person is wanted in connection with a nonbailable offence of grave nature isis not entitled to anticipatory bail. All persons charged with nonbailable offences must be treated equally unless of course there are special circumstances which need special consideration in the particular facts of a case. 

 Anticipatory bail should be granted by the High Court Division for a limited period or till filing of the charge-sheet, whichever is appropriate in the circumstance of the case. After expiry of the period of filing of the charge-sheet as the case may be the accused must appear before the court concerned and obtain fresh bail from the court on the merit of the 'case. Granting of anticipatory bail in an exceptional circumstance is a matter to be decided by the learned Judges on the facts of a particular case. The special and exceptional circumstances are to be left to the discretion of the learned Judges. 

 Power of granting anticipatory bail is somewhat extraordinary in character and it is only in exceptional cases such power is to be exercised. 

 Ordinarily, this court is loath to interfere with the orders of granting or refusing bail but it cannot be an insurmountable obstacle in the way of rectifying an order which tends to disclose miscarriage of justice. 

 31. The conspectus which emerges from the various authorities of Apex Courts is that anticipatory bail is an extraordinary remedy which can be granted only in exceptional and extraordinary circumstances upon a proper and intelligent exercise of discretion and upon facts and materials disclosed by the petitioner seeking anticipatory bail before court in a criminal proceeding which is being launched or has been launched against him with ulterior motive, political or otherwise, for causing harassment and humiliation to accused person and not for ends of justice. Anticipatory bail must be for a limited period/duration or till submission of charge-sheet and that will be dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each and every case, Anticipatory bail, thus, cannot be granted in all cases as a matter of course and has to be granted only in exceptional cases. The court when approached for anticipatory bail is to consider whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, judicial discretion should be exercised in favour of the person seeking anticipatory bail. 

 (c) Informant Syeda Tania, thereafter presented a petition of complaint before Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong beyond petitioner's knowledge and in the petition she brought allegation that the petitioner through acts of forgery obtained her signature in kabinnama and also in affidavit. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Chittagong by order dated 19-8-2001 sent the petition of complaint to officer-in-charge for investigation and after investigation to treat the same as First Information Report. Officer-in-charge Kulshi police station treated the petition of complaint as Non FIR (First Information Report) Case No. 263 of2001 corresponding to GDE No. 1554 dated 28- 8-2001 arising out of Non GR Case No. 2033 of 2001. 

 35. Syeda Tania in the capacity of informant laid a petition before this court for her addition as party in Criminal Miscellaneous Case. Informant Syeda Tania was not added as opposite party in the case but her learned Advocate was allowed' to appear in the case and have submission with learned Attorney-General or Deputy Attorney- General or Assistant Attorney-General representing the State at the time of hearing of Criminal Miscellaneous Case. 

 36. Informant Syeda Tania, although was not made an opposite party in the case yet submitted a counter-affidavit. In the counter-affidavit statements are made that petitioner created false affidavit and kabinnama which were beyond knowledge of informant and she filed a suit being Other Class Suit No. 99 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong challenging the said kabinnama and also laid complaint case being Non GR Case No. 2033 of 2001 in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. It is further stated that petitioner filed the suit being Family Suit No. 50 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong for restitution of conjugal life without the actual marriage and no harassment is caused to accused petitioner rather the complainant is being harassed. It is also, stated that Anticipatory Bail itself is a temporary measure for a short time and petitioner has already enjoyed the privilege of Anticipatory Bail even though he did not deserve to have anticipatory bail. 

 1.	Informant lodged the case at the instance of her father who is bent upon harassing and humiliating the petitioner and the petitioner is genuinely apprehensive of police harassment and in the event of his surrender before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong he would not get justice. 

 iv. 	Under the fact and circumstances of the case the petitioner got no other forum than to surrender before the High Court Division wherefrom he can get justice. 

 42. The positive case of the petitioner is that marriage between him and informant took place on 27-3-2001 and Affidavits were sworn by both petitioner and informant Syeda Tania before Notary Public and Mr. AKM Zahirul Haq, Advocate identified deponent-informant Syeda Tania and petitioner Patwary Rafiquddin Haider and Affidavits were counter-signed by Magistrate, First Class, Chittagong. Learned Advocate Mr. AKM Zahirul Hug in affidavit sworn by deponent Syeda Tania stated that deponent was known to him and she put her signature in his presence. Affidavit has been annexed as Annexure-B to the petition. The marriage was thereafter solemnised through a kabinnama dated 27-3-2001 by the Marriage Registrar. Annexure-C is copy of kabinnama. Informant Syeda Tania having not been an opposite party was not entitled to file counter-affidavit. But in the interest of justice and to come to a just decision counter-affidavit is being considered. In paragraph No. 34 of counter-affidavit it is stated that the petitioner created false affidavit and kabinnama beyond her knowledge and she filed a suit being Other Class Suit No. 99 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong challenging the kabinnama and complaint case being Non GR Case No. 2033 of 2001 had been filed in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 43. We shall now have a bird's eye view of the accusation launched against the petitioner in the petition of complaint which has been thereafter, registered as Kulshi Police Station Non FIR Case No. 263 of 2001 under sections 465/467/468/469/471/506 and 34 of the Penal Code. Accusation mounted against the petitioner is that no marriage was solemnised between petitioner and informant and informant did not put any signature on affidavit and did not go to the office of Marriage Register and petitioner created forged kabinnama forging the signature of informant and thus, committed forgery. From Counter-Affidavit it appears that informant had already instituted Other Class Suit No. 99 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong whereon kabinnama has been challenged as forged. Whether kabinnama has been created through acts of forgery or not will be adjudicated in the Other Class suit. Over the alleged creation of Kabinnama through forgery criminal proceeding in hand has been initiated. Subject matter of Other Class suit and criminal proceeding is same. 

 45. The ground and contentions pressed into service from the side of the petitioner that the criminal proceeding against the petitioner has been launched with ulterior motive to cause harassment to the petitioner and not for furthering the ends of justice cannot be ruled out and the .grounds and contentions appear to have substance. Exceptional and special circumstances for being graced with anticipatory bail have been made out by the petitioner. Judicial discretion is required to be exercised in granting anticipatory bail to him. Contentions advanced from the side of informant which was adopted by State-opposite party merit no consideration in view of fact and circumstances of the case and materials placed. 

 46. This takes us to Case-laws on which both sides put reliance. Before adverting to the case- laws it is to be borne in mind that a decision or judgment is only an authority for what it actually decides. It cannot be quoted for a proposition that may seem to follow from it. Every decision or judgment must be read applicable in the fact and circumstances of each and every case. It is neither desirable nor permissible to pick out a word or sentence from the Judgment divorced from the context of the question under consideration and treat it to be complete law declared by Court. The Judgment might be read as a whole and the observation from the Judgment has to be considered in the light of the questions which were before the court. A decision of a court takes its colour from the questions involved in the case in which it is rendered and while applying a decision to a later case court must carefully try to ascertain the true principle laid down by the Court to support the reasoning. 

 47. The case-laws placed from the side of petitioner are dealt with first. In State vs MA Malik 47 DLR (AD) 33. Accused-respondent MA Malik was admittedly married to one Sultana Yesmin Khan (Shaopa) daughter of Abdul Mukit Khan of Sylhet Town. Sultana Yesmin Khan filed a case against the respondent that the latter demanded dowry. The lady also instituted a suit being Family Suit No.14 of 1993 in the Family Court, Sadar Sylhet for dissolution of marriage. Accused- respondent moved before High Court Division for anticipatory bail. High Court Division granted anticipatory bail to accused-respondent. The order granting anticipatory bail to accused-respondent had been challenged by State as petitioner in criminal petition for leave to appeal before Appellate Division. Appellate Division considered facts and circumstances of the case and dismissed the petition adopting the view that the spouses were at logger-heads both having recourse to court and there was possibility of the respondent husband being harassed and it was difficult to hold that the High Court Division had granted bail unreasonably or unfairly. The Appellate Division found no compelling reason to interfere with the order of the High Court Division. 

 48. In Shabeebul Hasan and another vs State 22 DLR (Karachi) 216 a Bank Account opening form was allegedly forged and petitioner had been depicted as forger. Anticipatory bail was sought before High Court at Karachi for the petitioner. The High Court at Karachi granted anticipatory bail to petitioner. In granting anticipatory bail it was held that document allegedly forged ex facie did not show any tampering nor indicate any forgery and there are no other materials on record to support the allegation and accused has made out a prima facie case to be entitled to anticipatory bail before arrest. 

 49. In State vs MA Malik, 47 DLR (AD) 33 Anticipatory Bail was granted to accused MA Malik taking into account the nature of the accusation launched against him and also that the spouses were at logger-heads and suit between the parties were pending in court and also, fact and circumstances of the case. In the case in hand petitioner and the informant are also, at logger- heads and suits are pending in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong. The above cited case carries bearing in the fact and circumstances of the case in hand. In Shabeebul Hasan and another vs State, 22 DLR (Karachi) 216 High Court, Karachi granted anticipatory bail to accused- adopting the view that document allegedly forged by accused did not show any tampering nor indicate any forgery and there were no other material on record to support the allegation. Allegation against the petitioner before us is that he forged affidavit and kabinnama and the alleged act of forgery has become subject matter of a suit in the Second Court of Assistant Judge at Chittagong. The fact and circumstances of the above case appear to be quite applicable in the fact and circumstances of the present case. 

 50. Let us now turn to the case-laws referred to from the side of informant. In State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury and another 51 DLR (AD) 242=4 MLR (AD) 291 laws and principles regulating grant or refusal of anticipatory bail have been well settled and laws and principles settled in the above case have been set out in the foregoing paragraph and need not be stated again. In the above case one Md.Shahidul Islam was abducted and thereafter killed by persons named in the First Information Report and respondent Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury and another had been named as accused in the First Information Report. High Court Division granted anticipatory bail to accused respondents. State as petitioner/appellant before the Appellate Division prayed for definition and scope of Anticipatory Bail under section 498 of the Code. The accused respondent Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury stood indicted for offence punishable under section 302 of Penal Code and the offence was grave and serious in nature. The Appellate Division took the view that when a person is wanted in connection with non- bailable offence of grave nature he is not entitled to anticipatory bail. Appellate Division found that accused respondent could not make out any exceptional and special circumstances for grant of anticipatory bail by High Court Division and wrongly passed the order granting anticipatory bail to accused respondent. 

 51. In Pokar Ram vs State of Rajasthan, AIR 1985 (SC) 969 the accused Chandan Singh stood indicted for commission of murder of one Bhanwaria by gunshot and offence was under section 302 of the Penal Code. Anticipatory bail was sought for accused Chandan Singh before High Court of Rajasthan and anticipatory bail was granted to accused Chandan Singh. The order granting anticipatory bail was challenged from the side of State before the Supreme Court of India. Supreme Court considered Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia vs State of Punjab, AIR 1980 (SC) 1632 and principles enunciated therein. Supreme Court of India held that accusation against the accused respondent is that he has committed an offence of murder under section 302 of the Penal Code and when a person is accused of an offence of murder by the use of a firearm, the court has to be very careful and circumspect in entertaining an application for anticipatory bail. In the case, deceased Bhanwaria was gunned down by accused Chandan Singh and be stood charged for an offence under section 302 of the Penal Code. Supreme Court of India taking into account the gravity and seriousness of crime cancelled the bail of accused Chandan Singh. 

 52. In State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury and another 51 DLR AD 242=4 MLR (AD) 291 accused respondent had been under indictment for offence punishable under section 302 of the Penal Code and the offence was serious and grave in nature. No exceptional and special circumstances could be made out by accused respondent to be favoured with anticipatory bail and, as such, order of the High Court Division granting anticipatory bail stood set aside by the Appellate Division. In the case in hand the petitioner has bet." made an accused for alleged acts of forgery in creating affidavit and kabinnama and the subject matter of Criminal Proceeding has become, also, a subject matter of a suit in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong and the petitioner and informant are at loggerheads. Exceptional and special circumstances appear to have existed for granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner. In Pokar Ram vs State of Rajasthan, AIR 1985 SC 969 the accused Chandan Singh, also stood arraigned for offence punishable under section 302 of Penal Code as he gunned down the deceased and the offence was grave and serious and taking into account the seriousness and gravity of offence anticipatory bail granted to accused Chandan Singh had been cancelled by the Supreme Court. Special circumstances existed for cancelling anticipatory bail of accused Chandan Singh. The facts and circumstances of cited cases got no manner of applicability in the fact and circumstances of the case in hand and informant cannot take any aid of the cited cases. 

 53. Regard being had to the fact that informant Syeda Tania as plaintiff on 1-2-2001 has instituted a suit being Other Class Suit No. 99 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, Chittagong against the petitioner as defendant challenging Kabinnama and that the present criminal proceeding is launched against the petitioner by informant on the accusation of alleged forgery committed by petitioner and the subject matter of Other Class Suit and Criminal Proceeding laid by informant against the petitioner has been same and that the petitioner as plaintiff also, laid a suit being Family Suit No. 50 of 2001 in the Second Court of Assistant Judge, and also, Family Court, Chittagong against informant as defendant for Decree of Restitution of Conjugal Right and that the petitioner and informant are at loggerheads, facts and attending circumstances of the whole matter and the Authoritative pronouncement of the Apex Courts referred to above and gamut of the whole legal perspects, we are of the considered and dispassionate view that it will be just and proper to exercise judicial discretion in granting Anticipatory Bail to the petitioner till submission of police report on completion of investigation to be performed by police in the event of registration of Non First Information Report Case into first information report case. The petitioner, thus, is granted Anticipatory Bailon bail bond furnished by him earlier till submission of police report on completion of investigation by police. The petitioner shall not in any way intimidate, hamper and interfere in the course of free and fair investigation nor influence any witness. In the event of submission of charge-sheet against petitioner he shall surrender to the regular Court i.e. the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong, and Chief Metropolitan Magistrate shall consider bail matter on materials placed before him and also in consonance with laws and principles regulating grant or refusal of bail and uninfluenced by any observation made in this Judgment.
